key_idea: In a unicyclic graph tree edges are forced iff some pair is split by them; on the cycle a set of removed edges is valid iff no pair separates two of them, i.e. the removed edges all have the same set of pairs covering them, detectable by XOR hashing.
sketch: Give each pair a random 64-bit value XORed onto both endpoints. Peel leaves: a tree edge is kept iff the subtree XOR is nonzero, and the XOR is pushed to the parent. On the remaining cycle c0..c(m-1), the edge after c_i gets the prefix XOR of the accumulated values; edges with equal hash can all be deleted together, so the answer is forced tree edges + cycle total - max weight sum of one hash class. O(n + k) expected with a hash map. Pitfalls: more than one cycle edge may be removed (the class with hash 0 are edges no pair needs), pairs inside one hanging tree cancel out automatically, sums need 64-bit. Stress-tested against a subset brute force.
